text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Parliament investigation committee demands explanation from Macedonian government how 400 million German marks from the state budget were spend for the needs of the government and several ministries in the first three months last year.
- Macedonia and Croatia signed a free trade agreement in Zagreb on Wednesday. Customs taxes to decrease, trade to double and joint ventures on third markets expected.

- Macedonian and Yugoslav agriculture ministers, Nikola Parakeov and Nedeljko Sipovac, signed on Wednesday in Skopje three agreements on cooperation in the fields of plant protection, veterinarian practice and science.

- Macedonia's ruling SDAM party central committee officially states that "the situation in the country is unfavourable and additionally complicated with the bankruptcy of the TAT savings institution from Bitola".

- Ninety-two people infected with bruccelosis in Macedonia. Alarming situation in the Tetovo village Germo where 42 people have contracted the disease. Four cases registered in Skopje. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
